chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Khalid al-Maraghi reported to me from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Hammad, who reported from Ubaid ibn Ya’eesh, who reported from Yunus ibn Bukair, who reported from Yahya ibn Abi Hayyah Abu Janab al-Kalbi, from Abu al-Aliyah, who said: I heard Abu Umamah say: The Messenger of God, peace be upon him and his family, said:

"There are six great virtues. Whoever acts upon any one of them, it will argue on his behalf on the Day of Judgment until it enters him into Paradise, saying: O Lord, this person used to act upon me in the worldly life. They are: prayer, almsgiving, pilgrimage, fasting, fulfilling trusts, and maintaining family ties."

key_terms.جادلت: Argued, pleaded (personifying the deed as an advocate)
key_terms.سِتّ: Six, referring to six fundamental virtues or deeds

ai.seo_question: What are the six virtues that will intercede on the Day of Judgment according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) enumerated six fundamental acts of worship and moral conduct -- prayer, zakat, hajj, fasting, trustworthiness, and maintaining kinship ties -- teaching that any single one of them, if practiced, will serve as an intercessor for its doer on the Day of Judgment, pleading before God until that person enters Paradise. This hadith was delivered as a prophetic exhortation to the companions, emphasizing that these acts are not passive rituals but living advocates that testify on behalf of the believer.
